console.model_source: owner manual confirmation; PTP DeviceInfo reports the generic model 'Nintendo Switch'
console.modification_source: owner report; PTP does not detect modifications

method.summary: A DNS responder answered every A query with the Mac's LAN address and an HTTP server redirected unknown paths to a local page. The console's captive-portal check connected, the WifiWebAuthApplet opened, and the page posted a JavaScript fingerprint back to the server.
method.console_change: Temporary manual primary DNS entry pointing at the Mac; reverted by the owner afterwards.
method.privileges_required: Root on the Mac to bind DNS port 53 and HTTP port 80.

network_flow: DNS query for ctest.cdn.nintendo.net, answered with the Mac's address
HTTP GET / from 192.168.178.136 with User-Agent 'NX NIFM/00', redirected
HTTP GET / from the same client with the WifiWebAuthApplet user agent, redirected
HTTP GET /portal served the fingerprint page
HTTP POST /fp delivered the fingerprint JSON

browser.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Nintendo Switch; WifiWebAuthApplet) AppleWebKit/613.0 (KHTML, like Gecko) NF/6.0.3.31.11 NintendoBrowser/5.1.0.55481

interpretation: The captive-portal applet is reachable without credentials and executes attacker-supplied JavaScript, which makes it a genuine stage-1 surface. The User-Agent is not a build identifier. Feature detection brackets the engine to Safari 15.4-15.6 (WebKit 615.x, 2022). The applet has no URL whitelist and allows ignoring invalid TLS certificates. Web-applet NPDM grants fsp-srv, nvdrv:a, hid:sys, ssl, bsd:a and SystemSaveData access, so a compromise would be a real userland foothold. The security patch level remains unknown, and the documented absence of a JIT invalidates many public WebKit techniques.
limitations: One console, one applet, one session.
The User-Agent token does not identify the WebKit build, and the feature set only bounds it to ES2020 or later.
The observed applet is the captive-portal applet. Other applets such as WebApplet or the account login flow may use a different build and a URL whitelist.
Reachability and JavaScript execution are not evidence of a vulnerability.
The fingerprint page ran with the console's DNS temporarily pointed at the host; no console setting was permanently changed.
redactions: The console's LAN address is recorded in the local JSONL only as a subnet peer and is omitted here.

deep_fingerprint.note: Second pass using scripts/fingerprint_deep.html. Feature booleans are direct results; string values are typeof/eval results.
deep_fingerprint.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Nintendo Switch; WifiWebAuthApplet) AppleWebKit/613.0 (KHTML, like Gecko) NF/6.0.3.31.11 NintendoBrowser/5.1.0.55481

engine_bracket.caveat: Feature detection does not establish the security patch level; Nintendo can backport fixes without adding features.
